items.title: What Every Home Needs for an Extended Power Outage
items.summary:
Americans are “pantry-loading” following a cascade of technology outages that have disrupted email, grounded flights, and interrupted banking services—while feuling fears that the failures could be signs of something bigger .

Costco and Walmart have reported increased purchases of emergency supplies, from food and water to batteries and generators. As of Nov. 15, 21 of the 26 high-priced generators offered on Costco's website were sold out, according to Bloomberg .

"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales," David Bellinger , an analyst for Mizuho , a Japanese investment bank, wrote in a recent research note.

Federal officials say they've found no evidence that the outages are connected or resulted from coordinated cyberattacks. But while the fears driving the rush to stockpile may be unfounded, the threat of prolonged disruptions is all-too real.

In August, severe storms knocked out power to nearly 375,000 customers across Northwest Indiana , leaving some without electricity for nearly two weeks.

A historic ice storm in January caused more than 330,000 outages across Mississippi and Louisiana , where some residents faced similarly long waits.

Both emergencies stretched far beyond the familiar three-day supply of food and water—and exposed how quickly households can lose access to basic necessities.

“A three-day emergency kit is still a good starting point, but I’d consider it the minimum…
items.t: What Every Home Needs for an Extended Power Outage

items.title: Mortgage Rates Surge Again as Stubborn Inflation Ends Brief Reprieve
items.summary:
Mortgage rates are rising again after four consecutive weeks of declines, as hotter-than-anticipated inflation data sets the stage for another interest rate hike, putting upward pressure on Treasury yields. 

The average rate on 30-year fixed home loans jumped to 7.28% for the week ending Nov. 19, up 17 basis points from 7.11% recorded the week before, according to Freddie Mac . For perspective, rates averaged 6.26% one year ago.

"While prospective borrowers often shop around for a home, they may not always think to do the same for their mortgage, as comparing multiple rate quotes can potentially save them thousands over a loan's lifetime," says Sam Khater , Freddie Mac's chief economist.

The October Consumer Price Index (CPI) report came in above expectations last week on both the headline and core measures, all but guaranteeing that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark rate to curb inflation at the next Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Dec. 8. 

The looming hike, combined with the persistence of the war in Iran, pushed the 10-year Treasury yield back toward 5% this week, putting mortgage rates on an upward trajectory once again. 

"The debate has shifted from whether the Fed hikes in December to how aggressively it moves," says Realtor.com® senior economist Anthony Smith . "That is a tough backdrop for mortgage rates heading into what is already a seasonally slow stretch for the housing market."

Markets are currently pricing a 93% chance of a 25-basis-point increase next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Meanwhile, pending home sales…
items.t: Mortgage Rates Surge Again as Stubborn Inflation Ends Brief Reprieve

items.title: Damaged Building Next to Brooklyn Collapse Scene Will Be Demolished
items.summary:
A Brooklyn apartment building adjacent to the site of last week's deadly building collapse is set to be demolished after city officials determined that it was unsafe to enter.

On Nov. 11, the three-story mixed-use building at 1321 Flatbush Ave. suddenly collapsed, killing eight people, including two children, and injuring 18 others.

When 1321 Flatbush collapsed, it took the adjoining wall of 1323 Flatbush Ave. with it, leaving the apartments in that building exposed to the elements. Striking images from the scene showed the perfectly undisturbed apartment interiors of 1323 Flatbush just as tenants had left them as they rushed to escape. 

The collapse occurred while workers were doing excavation work at 2625 Bedford Ave., adjacent to 1321 Flatbush—a job site that had a history of safety violations, including proceeding with demolition in defiance of a stop-work order, according to the Department of Buildings.

The city has opened an investigation into the cause of the collapse and is doing sweeps of more than 160 work sites across the city associated with the construction team at 2625 Bedford Ave.

”If there is anyone or any entity operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable," New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a press conference last week.

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez has also opened a criminal inquiry into the collapse. No charges have been filed yet.

Displaced tenants of both buildings are staying in hotels provided by the American Red Cross through the end of November and the Department of…
items.t: Damaged Building Next to Brooklyn Collapse Scene Will Be Demolished

items.title: ‘Vanderpump Rules’ Star Jax Taylor Reveals Secret Cancer Battle—Inside the L.A. Home Where He’ll Recover
items.summary:
Jax Taylor had been quietly facing one of the most frightening chapters of his life while settling into a new home with his son, Cruz . 

Now, after revealing that doctors found cancer in his left kidney, the "Vanderpump Rules" alum is looking ahead to recovery following a five-hour surgery to remove the tumor.

Taylor, 47, took to Instagram on Nov. 18, to share his diagnosis, explaining that the discovery came after he was hospitalized with kidney stones in July. 

A CT scan also showed a tumor on his left kidney. After a series of tests and appointments, he learned it was cancer—a revelation he had kept private for months.

"This is something I’ve kept private for the past few months because it’s been one of the scariest times of my life. Back in July, I woke up one morning in horrible pain and ended up in the hospital with kidney stones. What I thought was just a kidney stone turned into something I never imagined," he penned on his candid social media post. 

Jax Taylor had been quietly facing one of the most frightening chapters of his life while settling into a new home with his son, Cruz. (Instagram) 

He added, "My CT scan also showed a tumor on my left kidney. After many tests and appointments I found out it was cancer. I lost my father to cancer, so hearing that word just broke me. It put me in a really dark place. The hardest part was the waiting. Knowing there was a tumor growing inside me while trying to go about my life like everything was fine. It’s crazy how you can act like everything is normal when deep down you’re a mess." 

The reality TV star revealed…
items.t: ‘Vanderpump Rules’ Star Jax Taylor Reveals Secret Cancer Battle—Inside the L.A. Home Where He’ll Recover

items.title: Family Found Dead in Foreclosed Home Survived Months Longer Than Previously Thought
items.summary:
New evidence suggests that at least one member of a family found dead inside a foreclosed-upon Connecticut home survived longer than previously thought—paving the way for transfer of title to a new owner. 

The bizarre case hinges upon whether the home's owners died before or after the foreclosure was recorded. If the owners were already dead at the time of the filing, the foreclosure may be deemed illegitimate, and a search for rightful heirs would begin.

Edward Marchion stumbled into the mystery in June, when he purchased 7 Stanwich Lane , a four-bedroom, three-bathroom home in Burlington, CT , in a foreclosure auction for $525,000. The 2,800-square-foot home sits on more than 2 acres and comes with a hot tub, patio, and deck, according to the listing.

A few days after placing the winning bid, Marchion finally entered the property and came across a grisly sight. The skeletal remains of the property’s previous owners, Sally Anne Cash and Paul Cash , and their adult son Brian Cash , were found inside. 

Marchion then asked a judge to halt the closing on the property to determine the timeline of the Cashs’ deaths. 

In a July 2 filing in the state Supreme Court, Marchion’s lawyer John C. Lewis III asked the court to delay closing until the Connecticut State Police could determine whether the Cash family died before or after the foreclosure action.

"From a title perspective, unless it can be determined that the Defendants were alive on the date the lis pendens was recorded (August 6, 2025), then the foreclosure action is defective," wrote Lewis.

Now, months later, new…
items.t: Family Found Dead in Foreclosed Home Survived Months Longer Than Previously Thought

items.title: Anthropic’s Blockbuster IPO Set To Spark a New San Francisco Housing Frenzy: ‘Expect More All-Cash Offers’ and Bidding Wars
items.summary:
Real estate agents in San Francisco are bracing for further acceleration of the housing market as Anthropic makes an initial public offering at a reported valuation of $1.5 trillion.

The Bay Area has been a hot spot for newly wealthy AI trendsetters in recent years, rebuilding a market that was left hurting during the COVID-19 pandemic as tech offices emptied. With major AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic planting roots in San Francisco, the housing market has grown competitive, leading what some real estate agents are calling a “ mansion shortage .”

Anthropic’s highly anticipated IPO went live on Thursday, marking one of the largest public-market debuts in history.

The Claude developer, which will trade under the ticker ANT, initially said it planned to price shares at between $70 and $78, which would value the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.45 trillion. Late Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal reported the company planned to debut at $83 per share, taking the valuation to $1.5 trillion.

In addition to the public offering, Anthropic is set to receive an extra $26 billion in a private placement sale of shares to several other major tech companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, and more, according to Yahoo Finance .

While employees and insiders won't see cash in hand until after a significant lockup period, the debut could give many early shareholders the confidence to move forward with real estate purchases.

“Confidence may change before purchasing power does. There are lockup periods, taxes, and individual circumstances to consider, so I…
items.t: Anthropic’s Blockbuster IPO Set To Spark a New San Francisco Housing Frenzy: ‘Expect More All-Cash Offers’ and Bidding Wars

items.title: Anthropic’s Backers Have Another Big Bet: Americans Staying Renters
items.summary:
Anthropic’s stock market debut on Thursday is expected to value the artificial intelligence company at $1.5 trillion, putting some of Wall Street’s biggest investment firms in line to cash in from its rapid rise .

In its pitch to investors , the maker of Claude offers a vision far grander than the 2,800 millionaires the IPO is expected to mint. AI, it says, could “significantly accelerate global growth and dramatically improve quality of life for people around the world.”

But some of its backers are making another bet on a future where renting dominates the housing market .

Among them are Blackstone and Brookfield , two investment giants whose portfolios extend from emerging technologies to the nation's housing stock. 

“Amidst continued macroeconomic uncertainty, we believe rental housing is the number one thing you want to own,” reads a 2025 shareholder update from Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust, known as BREIT.

Under a heading touting Blackstone Real Estate’s “Best Ideas,” the fund pointed to record homeownership costs, sluggish construction, and a national shortage of 4 million to 5 million homes . It called those conditions “powerful tailwinds” for its rental housing investments.

To housing advocates, though, those tailwinds are precisely the headwinds they’re working to reverse, says Jordan Ash , housing director at the nonprofit watchdog Private Equity Stakeholder Project.

Heads or tails? It depends on whom you ask 

The investment thesis anticipates a future in which “there are many more people who are just going to be renters for life,” Ash tells…
items.t: Anthropic’s Backers Have Another Big Bet: Americans Staying Renters

items.title: You Can Order Room Service From This $29.5 Million Full-Floor Ritz-Carlton Residence on Central Park South
items.summary:
A $29.5 million residence spanning an entire floor of the Ritz-Carlton Hotel has hit the market in New York City .

Measuring 5,724 square feet—which is nearly three times the median in its ZIP code— Residence 29 at 50 Central Park South is one of the city’s “most prestigious addresses,” according to listing agent Zina Raslan of the Gambino Group at Compass .

The five-bedroom, five-plus-bathroom dwelling is one of only a dozen permanent residences exclusive to the hotel . And while it’s accessible through a private elevator vestibule, it offers a unique perk that’s also available to Ritz-Carlton guests.

“You can order room service from your very own home,” Raslan confirmed.

With ample east- and west-facing windows found throughout the home, the skyline and Central Park views are absolutely spectacular. There are even two private terraces that look over the park—one for dining and one for lounging.

“These spaces give you a reason to really pause and enjoy the setting of New York City,” Raslan said, conjuring ideas of “morning coffee overlooking the greenery of Central Park” or “dinner outside as the lights change.”

The building originally opened in 1930 as the Hotel St. Moritz, designed by Emery Roth , the architect behind The San Remo and the Beresford. In 2002, it was reimagined as the Ritz-Carlton, with an exclusive collection of private residences above the hotel.

items.title: Inside Celebrity Chef Dook Chase’s Renovated New Orleans Home—and the Dream Kitchen He Calls His Sanctuary
items.summary:
Celebrity chef Dook Chase is intentionally never far from a kitchen, be it inside one of his renowned restaurants or his dream family home in New Orleans . 

Chase, 44, is the fourth-generation owner of Dooky Chase’s Restaurant, the legendary culinary destination and cultural institution that’s been operating in the Big Easy since 1941. The NOLA native also runs his modern Creole eatery, Chapter IV, commuting between both businesses from a Southern-style, two-story residence that he shares with his wife, Gretchen , their daughter, Sidne y , and son, Vito . 

“It's a seven-minute commute to both restaurants,” Chase tells Realtor.com® in the latest Celebrity Sanctuary . “I can visit each one in its peak time. I can get a text from any server saying, ‘Hey, a table came in that really wanted to see you,’ and I [say], ‘Tell them I'll be there in seven minutes.’ I can hop in the car and get to each.”  

Personally connecting with the local community over a meal is a practice that is baked into Chase’s family backstory and a tradition he proudly upholds today. 

“When you think about Dooky Chase Restaurant and my grandmother, chef Leah Chase , in the time that she helmed that kitchen ... the history of our restaurant is really through the Civil Rights Movement, opening doors to everyone in the community: Blacks and whites, together, at a time when laws didn't allow it. But we always allowed it at our restaurant,” the Le Cordon Bleu-educated executive chef explains. “My grandparents, great-grandparents, [and] certainly my parents understood the importance of learning from each and…
items.t: Inside Celebrity Chef Dook Chase’s Renovated New Orleans Home—and the Dream Kitchen He Calls His Sanctuary

items.title: West Virginia Official Accused of Stealing 9 Properties for Friend With Ties to His Used Car Dealership
items.summary:
A West Virginia state auditor has been indicted for his role in an alleged scheme to steal nine properties from their owners and sell them to benefit a longtime friend and business associate—who also owns the land where the official operated a used car dealership.

Mark Hunt , 66, is accused of using his position as a state official to improperly transfer several tax-delinquent properties to a real estate company owned by the wife of his friend, Charleston attorney Robert Johns , despite the warnings of other state employees that such transactions violated state law.

Federal prosecutors announced on Monday that a federal grand jury had indicted Hunt, Johns, and three employees of the State Auditor’s Office in connection with the alleged scheme, alleging the group bypassed legal requirements to transfer ownership of properties located in Kanawha and Boone counties.

The charges against Hunt come on the heels of a West Virginia Watch investigation that revealed his used car dealership, After Hours Used Auto, operated on land owned by Johns' company, NAJ LLC.

The 9 property transfers that raised red flags 

At the center of the alleged scheme were nine properties in Kanawha and Boone counties whose owners were behind on their property taxes.

Under state law, tax-delinquent properties can eventually be transferred to investors who meet certain legal requirements. But prosecutors allege those requirements were ignored in this case.

A real estate company called MAPA Inc., owned by Johns' wife, Patricia Johns , attempted to purchase the properties, according to West Virginia…

items.title: Resident of Collapsed Brooklyn Building Sues for Negligence After Losing $100K Record Collection
items.summary:
The first of what is likely to be several lawsuits was filed in Kings County Superior Court on Monday, alleging widespread negligence by a host of landlords, construction companies, and contractors in last week's deadly Brooklyn building collapse .

Dengane Omari Jack lived at 1321 Flatbush Ave., which collapsed last Wednesday, tragically killing eight people and wounding 18 more. "He was one of the lucky ones," a friend wrote on a GoFundMe campaign to support Jack. "But surviving came at an unimaginable cost: in a matter of seconds, he lost his home, everything he owned, and a lifetime's worth of memories and work."

Now, Jack is suing his landlord and management company, as well as a half-dozen companies affiliated with 2625 Bedford Ave. , the lot adjacent to his Flatbush building. None of those entities has filed a response to the complaint yet in court.

According to the lawsuit: “During October 2026, Plaintiff observed cracks at or near the Building's entrance, photographed those cracks, and reported the condition to the landlord or management responsible for the Building.”

items.title: Florida Homes Are Flooding in the Dry Season—and Too Many Owners Are Unprepared
items.summary:
The Sunshine State is facing an unusual bout of heavy rain and flooding in the middle of its dry season, which usually begins in November. 

The unexpected weather has put pressure on drainage systems and left standing water in many communities, particularly those in South Florida’s Broward County and along Central Florida’s Atlantic Coast in places like Daytona Beach and Cape Canaveral .

On Nov. 18, the western part of Broward County faced what meteorologists refer to as a “rain bomb.” In just 24 hours, West Hollywood received over 15 inches of rain , while surrounding neighborhoods saw about 10 inches. 

Due to the severity of the situation, which has led to issues such as stranded cars and out-of-service traffic signals, Broward County and Hollywood declared states of emergency , with Hollywood officials encouraging residents to shelter in place and avoid unnecessary travel . 

Forecasters expect additional rainfall through the end of this week as well as 2 to 4 inches across Eastern Florida, with about 4 to 8 inches from Miami to Jacksonville between Tuesday and Friday. Some areas may even get hit with up to 12 inches.

While the wet and windy conditions are expected to improve, the Southeast may see a cooler, rainier Thanksgiving this year . The rain could linger from the upper coast of Texas toward the southern Atlantic Coast throughout the holiday weekend.

“The dry season doesn’t mean your house is in the clear. Florida is currently showing us that heavy rain can flood homes miles from the beach,” says John Espenschied , owner at InsuranceBrokers.com in O'Fallon,…
items.t: Florida Homes Are Flooding in the Dry Season—and Too Many Owners Are Unprepared

items.title: In Portland, OR, Entry-Level Buyers Suddenly Have More Options
items.summary:
A new metro-by-metro analysis from Realtor.com® reveals where buyers can still find a starter home . These options have felt increasingly scarce as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates create challenges for many would-be buyers.

According to research, the national share of starter homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. During that same period, starter home prices rose 30.8%, from about $260,000 to $340,000. 

However, some cities are bucking this trend, and Portland, OR , has seen an encouraging uptick in starter homes in recent years.

Portland sees a rise in starter homes 

A starter home is defined as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price, capturing the relative affordability of an area's lower-end market. These homes are typically smaller and less expensive, making them accessible to a first-time buyer or a household with an Income at or below the local median.

In the Portland-Vancouver, OR-WA , metro area, the share of starter homes has shown positive growth. The share was 28.0% in 2019 and dipped slightly to 27.8% in 2022 before rising to 32.0% in 2026. 

This represents a total increase of +4.0 percentage points since 2019, signaling growing opportunity for buyers in the market.

items.title: Oklahoma City, OK, Struggles With Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities
items.summary:
A recent metro-by-metro analysis by Realtor.com® reveals where buyers can still find a starter home . For many would-be homeowners, these options have felt increasingly scarce as rising prices and climbing mortgage rates compound affordability challenges.

Furthermore, research from economists supports this trend. Nationally, the share of starter homes in active inventory fell from 38.1% in August 2019 to 36.2% in August 2026. During that same period, starter home prices rose 30.8%, from roughly $260,000 to $340,000. 

As a result, some markets like Oklahoma City have experienced a downturn in available starter homes in recent years.

Starter home availability declines in Oklahoma City 

A starter home is typically defined as a property priced at roughly 80% of a metro's median list price. This captures the relative affordability of homes at the lower end of a local market. These homes are generally smaller and less expensive, making them accessible to a first-time buyer or a household with an Income at or below the area median.

In Oklahoma City, OK, the share of starter homes has seen a steady decline. The portion of these homes was 34.8% in 2019, which then decreased to 33.1% in 2022. As of 2026, the share has fallen further to 31.4%.

Therefore, this represents a total decrease of 3.4 percentage points between 2019 and 2026. This trend indicates a shrinking market for entry-level homes in the area, presenting a challenge for new buyers.

items.t: Oklahoma City, OK, Struggles With Low Starter Home Availability Compared to Other Cities

items.title: Fed Officials Expect Further Interest Rate Hikes After Pausing Last Month
items.summary:
Leaders at the Federal Reserve held firm on interest rates in October, but also thought a future rate hike "would likely be appropriate" as some mulled a larger hike in December, according to meeting minutes released on Wednesday.

At the Oct. 27–28 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), policymakers voted 10-2 to keep the overnight rate at its previous 3.75%-4.00% range. The decision came days before the 2026 midterms, even as FOMC members agreed inflation was a persistent concern.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh joined the majority, while Fed Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both voted in favor of a quarter-point increase. One month before, the FOMC voted to raise rates for the first time in three years in an effort to clamp down on inflation. 

The minutes—which don't name FOMC members specifically while discussing their deliberations—show that some of the FOMC members considered that, while the impact of tariffs on the economy was waning, high energy costs continue to pressure Americans. 

Indeed, some participants even noted that, if the inflation numbers got too unfavorable, they would consider a rate hike of more than a quarter-percent in December. Bond markets still view that as unlikely, with the probability of a larger half-point hike next month at just 5%, according to CME FedWatch .

Still, Federal Reserve Gov. Christopher Waller told CNBC on Wednesday it may be necessary to "shock people" with a larger rate hike. He said in a speech this month that a half-percent point hike might be necessary next month.

items.t: Fed Officials Expect Further Interest Rate Hikes After Pausing Last Month

items.title: The Thanksgiving Hosting Stress Test: Is Your Place Ready for the Big Day?
items.summary:
Hosting Thanksgiving in your first home is exciting, but it can also feel overwhelming. 

“You likely want everything to look and feel ‘put together’ as soon as possible despite the fact that a fresh move-in is typically anything but,” says Kate Pechinka , founder and principal designer of Kate Kelly Interiors in Chester Springs, PA .

The pressures of living up to the warm environment you’ve either experienced growing up or seen in movies or advertisements combined with the added demands on your home’s systems don’t make things any easier. 

“Suddenly, multiple people are using the bathrooms, the dishwasher and garbage disposal are running frequently, the oven is working for hours, and guests are moving through spaces that may not have been arranged for entertaining,” explains Kevin Vander Hyde , vice president of Vander Hyde Services in Grand Rapids, MI .

Here’s the good news: With a little preparation and planning, you can ensure your home is Thanksgiving-ready and alleviate a great deal of stress long before your guests arrive.

items.title: Private renters in England: have you struggled to get your deposit back?
items.summary:
We would like to hear from private tenants about their experiences of the rental deposit system in England

In May 2026, the government overhauled private renting by abolishing no-fault evictions and shifting private tenancies to rolling contracts. However, deposit protection remains an issue for many private renters.

The government has promised and begun consulting on reforms, including scrapping insured deposit schemes, but has yet to confirm when this will happen. Landlords and letting agents are currently permitted to hold tenant deposits in their own bank accounts and this creates a “power imbalance”, housing and planning minister Matthew Pennycook has said.
